text: FIGURE LEGEND
Figure 1 - Map of the protected nearshore zone off of Point
Cabrillo which constituted the study area. Habitat
boundaries are shown.
Figure 2 - Graph of the average density of the five primary
Embiotocid species found in the entire study area.
Density measured in fish per 10 square meters.
Figure 3 - Graph of the average density of each of the five
surfperrch in each respective habitat. Density measured
in fish per 10 square meters.
Figure 4 - Percent abundance measured solely by number of
fish observed in each habitat. Neither the size of the
habitats nor the differing total populations of the
species is taken into account.
Figure 5 - Correlation between the number of black surfperrch
observed under the railroad tracks and the height of
the tide. The line of regression was calculated and
drawn. Regression statistics presented in Table 8.
Figure 6 - Correlation between the number of reef surfperrch
observed in the area protected by Seal Rocks and the
height of the tide. The line of regression was
calculated and drawn. Regression statistics presented
in Table 8.
Figure 7 - Statistically unsignificant correlation between
the number of reef surfperrch observed in the channel
beyond Bird Rocks and the height of the tide.
Figure 8 - The density change of the surfperrch on Hopkins
Marine Life Reserve from 1979 to 1979. The 1979
densities are from Nichols (1979).
Figure 9 - The density change of the juvenile surfperrch of
three species of surfperrch on Hopkins Marine Life
Refuge from spring 1979 to spring 1989. The 1979
densities are from Nichols (1979).
